headline: Recalibrating Blanchard–Katz (1992) to 2026: the structural migration response to local unemployment has roughly halved (labor-force elasticity 0.0047→0.0022), and the model's fix is one declining migration parameter — the footprint of rising moving costs.

metrics.label: Migration elasticity to rel. unemployment (labor force)
metrics.note: −53%, ~7σ paper-era; independent structural confirmation of a weaker channel [ESTIMATED]

metrics.label: Year-1 out-migration share of adjustment (household)
metrics.note: adjustment rotated from migration toward job recovery [ESTIMATED]

metrics.label: Local-slump half-life, one-off shock
metrics.note: unchanged: falling migration m offset by rising job-recovery a [CALIBRATED]

metrics.label: Out-of-sample migration elasticity (fit pre-2015, test 2015–24)
metrics.note: 5× smaller out of sample; the decline is not an estimation-window artifact [ESTIMATED]

figures.caption: BK (1992) migration-adjustment model, original vs updated to 2026. A: direct FE migration responsiveness to local unemployment halved (labor force & population, rolling windows, paper-era stars). B: year-1 adjustment shifted away from out-migration (household 0.38→0.28, payroll 0.77→0.63). C: calibrated model UR impulse-response vs empirical AR(2) — the one-off half-life is unchanged (3 yr), but the GFC-window calibration lengthens it to 5 yr; the counterfactual restoring paper-era migration shortens it to 2.7 yr. D: empirical UR half-life is stable except a spike to 5 yr and deep cumulative troughs in the Great-Recession windows.
figures.alt: Four-panel figure: (A) two declining lines of migration responsiveness vs window-end year with a star at 1990; (B) stacked bars of adjustment shares for four era/basis groups; (C) decaying impulse-response curves with empirical points and a longer-decaying GFC curve; (D) a stable green half-life line with a GFC spike and a pink cumulative-unemployment line peaking around 2009.

notes: The directly-estimated migration elasticity is [ESTIMATED]; the two-margin (m,a) split is a stylized single-mode calibration ([CALIBRATED]) to the VAR migration share and UR half-life, used for the slump-duration counterfactual — not a newly estimated multi-equation IRF.

Honest tension with the premise: the one-off UR half-life did NOT lengthen — it resolves as a composition rotation (migration↓, job recovery↑); genuine lengthening is confined to severe/persistent shocks (GFC).

Minimal amendment = one declining migration-responsiveness parameter g_t (reduced-form of rising real moving costs / housing); an explicit house-price moving-cost margin was considered and rejected (needs unavailable state HPI; over-parameterized; observationally equivalent).
No new data downloaded; reused 001's panel and moments and the replication's AR→IRF engine. Baseline numbers read from paper.pdf and 001/results/estimates_by_window.csv.
